sources_checked: docs/creativity-screening/search/seed-verified-leads.md: Citation check of 33 leads from the first scan (2026-10-04)
coverage_limits: The report rechecks only the 33 leads from the first scan and gives sample sizes only where abstracts state them. ScienceDirect, INFORMS, HBS and Nature blocked direct access, so those records rest on Crossref, PubMed or RePEc data, and two points stay unverified: whether the published version of entry 4 keeps the variability finding, and the published abstract of entry 14.

candidates.title: Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs: Randomized Experiments on Divergent and Convergent Thinking
candidates.evidence: Two preregistered parallel experiments randomly assign participants to a standard LLM, a coach-like LLM, or no AI, followed by a final unassisted stage. The title names divergent and convergent thinking as the outcomes.

candidates.title: Human diversity fuels collective creativity that large language models cannot simulate or sustain
candidates.evidence: A preregistered experiment compares native and non-native English writers across three metaphor-writing arms (no AI, AI ideation, AI refinement), and the paper also simulates the writer pool with LLM personas. The report does not state N, the assignment method, or the outcome measures, and the title points to collective creativity.

candidates.title: The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI and Teamwork
candidates.task: professionals working alone or in two-person teams
candidates.evidence: Professionals in a preregistered field experiment are randomly assigned to AI or no AI and work alone or in two-person teams. The report does not state the task or a creativity outcome. N is 791 in the published abstract and 776 in NBER WP 33641 (April 2025), whose title ends '…Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise'. The report names only the first of 11 authors.

candidates.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
candidates.task: consultant tasks, including a shoe-idea task
candidates.evidence: Consultants in a preregistered experiment are randomly assigned to no AI, GPT-4, or GPT-4 plus a prompt-engineering overview. The 2023 working paper, whose title says 'AI' where the published one says 'Artificial Intelligence', reports a marked drop in the variability of AI users' shoe ideas compared with non-users. Neither abstract states this result, and the report could not confirm it in the published text. The report names only the first of 9 authors.

candidates.title: Creative scar without generative AI: Individual creativity fails to sustain while homogeneity keeps climbing
candidates.task: idea and solution generation over 7 days; Web of Science papers
candidates.evidence: Study 1 compares 419,344 Web of Science papers before and after ChatGPT-3.5. Study 2 is a 7-day lab experiment with two follow-ups in which half the participants used ChatGPT-4 (3,593 ideas, 427 solutions), and the title reports that individual creativity fails to last without AI while homogeneity keeps rising. The report does not state participant N or the assignment method. arXiv 2401.06816 is a precursor with a different title ('When ChatGPT is gone: Creativity reverts and homogeneity persists'), Liu as first author, 61 students and 3,302 ideas.

candidates.title: AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances
candidates.task: writing with AI suggestions, India and US
candidates.evidence: Participants in India and the US write with or without AI suggestions in a controlled experiment. The title reports that AI suggestions homogenize writing toward Western styles, and the report does not state the assignment method.

candidates.title: Can ChatGPT enhance business student creativity? Evidence from a randomised controlled trial
candidates.venue: Studies in Higher Education 51(7), 1432–1446 (2026 issue, online 2025)
candidates.evidence: A randomised controlled trial assigns business undergraduates in three disciplines to ChatGPT or no ChatGPT and compares their creativity. The article went online in 2025 and appears in a 2026 issue.

candidates.title: Large Language Model in Creative Work: The Role of Collaboration Modality and User Expertise
candidates.evidence: Experts and nonexperts write ads with an LLM as ghostwriter, with an LLM as sounding board, or without an LLM, and real ad clicks measure ad quality. The report does not state N or the assignment method.

candidates.title: Creative and Strategic Capabilities of Generative AI: Evidence from Large-Scale Experiments
candidates.task: creative tasks and a strategic game, US adults
candidates.evidence: The paper compares AI output with output from a representative sample of US adults and tests humans augmented with AI, using blind ratings and a strategic game. The report does not state N or the assignment method and found no published version.

candidates.title: Creativity and AI
candidates.venue: The Economic Journal, advance article (online 28 January 2026, no volume or issue yet)
candidates.evidence: Output from three ChatGPT versions is compared with human output on open and closed tasks, rated blind, and no arm has people using AI. N = 738 counts raters (4,428 evaluations).

candidates.title: Establishing the importance of co-creation and self-efficacy in creative collaboration with artificial intelligence
candidates.authors: McGuire, De Cremer, Van de Cruys
candidates.evidence: Two poetry-writing experiments compare writing alone, editing an AI poem, and co-creating with AI. The report does not state N, the assignment method, or the outcome measures.

candidates.title: Revolution or inflated expectations? Exploring the impact of generative AI on ideation in a practical sustainability context
candidates.evidence: The study compares AI-generated ideas with ideas from an expert workshop at BSH in a sustainability setting and adds a qualitative part. The report does not state N.

candidates.title: The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking
candidates.task: design ideation with an AI image generator
candidates.evidence: A between-participants experiment compares an AI image generator with a baseline condition, and the title names design fixation and divergent thinking as outcomes. The report does not state the assignment method.

candidates.title: ChatGPT improves creative problem-solving performance in university students: An experimental study
candidates.evidence: A preregistered experiment compares university students solving creative problems with ChatGPT (77) or without it (68). N comes from the preprint abstract because the published page was blocked, the report does not state the assignment method, and it names only the first of 7 authors.

candidates.title: Diverse AI personas can mitigate the homogenization effect in human-AI collaborative ideation
candidates.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans 8, 100289
candidates.task: story writing with AI persona plots
candidates.evidence: Ten AI personas generate 300 plots, and participants then write stories with or without access to them. The title reports that diverse personas can reduce homogenization, and the report does not state N or the assignment method.

candidates.title: Evaluating AI-assisted creative ideation: A crossover study in higher education
candidates.evidence: In a randomized crossover, design-engineering undergraduates alternate between ChatGPT-assisted and unaided tasks and produce 728 ideas. The report does not state the number of students.

candidates.title: Generative artificial intelligence, human creativity, and art
candidates.evidence: Observational platform data cover more than 4 million artworks from more than 50,000 users, and the title links generative AI, human creativity, and art. The report does not state the outcome measures or an exact user count.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence tools expand scientists' impact but contract science's focus
candidates.evidence: Observational analysis of 41.3 million papers relates AI tool use to scientists' impact and to the breadth of science's focus. The report warns that the paper covers AI tools across distinct eras of AI, not generative AI specifically.

candidates.title: Scientific production in the era of large language models
candidates.authors: Kusumegi, Yang, Ginsparg, de Vaan, Stuart, Yin
candidates.evidence: Observational analysis of 2.1 million preprints, 28,000 peer-review reports and 246 million accesses in the LLM era. The report does not state a creativity or diversity outcome, and it calls arXiv 2601.13187 an author version.

candidates.title: The rise of large language models and the direction and impact of US federal research funding
candidates.authors: Qian, Wen, Furnas, Bai, Shao, Wang
candidates.task: NSF and NIH proposals and awards
candidates.evidence: Observational analysis of NSF and NIH proposals from two universities plus all public awards, on how the rise of LLMs relates to the direction and impact of federal research funding. The report does not state a creativity or diversity outcome.

candidates.title: The shrinking landscape of linguistic diversity in the age of large language models
candidates.evidence: Three studies of more than 880,000 texts combine observational trends with LLM rewrites, and the title reports shrinking linguistic diversity in the LLM era. The report names only the first of 10 authors.

candidates.title: Scientific exploration, collaboration and labor division in the large language model era
candidates.evidence: Observational analysis of 775,323 scientists in the LLM era, covering the exploration, collaboration and labor division named in the title. The report does not state a creativity or diversity outcome.

candidates.title: Empirical evidence of Large Language Model's influence on human spoken communication
candidates.evidence: A synthetic-control analysis of 824,634 podcast episodes measures LLM influence on spoken communication, and a preregistered experiment adds N = 496. The report does not describe the experiment's conditions or a creativity or diversity outcome, and it notes that the first version listed 6 authors while the current one lists 10.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Creativity: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis
candidates.task: meta-analysis of generative AI and creativity studies
candidates.evidence: A meta-analysis of 28 studies with 8,214 participants reports g = 0.27 for with vs. without AI, g = −0.86 for diversity, and g = −0.05 for AI vs. humans. The report found no published version.

candidates.title: Has AI Surpassed Humans in Creative Idea Generation? A Meta-Analysis
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual Conference of the European Association of Cognitive Ergonomics (ECCE 2025), 1–11
candidates.task: meta-analysis of AI vs. human idea generation
candidates.evidence: A meta-analysis of 17 studies and 115 effect sizes compares AI output with human output in creative idea generation. A one-page conference abstract with a different title also exists (Biskjaer and de Rooij, 2025, 9th MIC Conference, Bolzano, no DOI), and the report treats this full paper as the citable version.

candidates.title: Does generative AI make us think alike? A systematic review and meta-analysis of homogenisation effects in human–AI co-creation
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenisation in human–AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies and 61 effect sizes asks whether human–AI co-creation makes creative output more homogeneous. The same meta-analysis appears as the ECCE 2026 short paper 'Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous' (pp. 198–201), whose abstract gives d = .334, while this journal abstract gives no d.

candidates.title: When combinations of humans and AI are useful: A systematic review and meta-analysis
candidates.evidence: A meta-analysis of 106 experiments on when combinations of humans and AI are useful. It covers AI broadly, not only generative AI, and the report does not state a creativity outcome.

candidates.title: Best humans still outperform artificial intelligence in a creative divergent thinking task
candidates.evidence: AI output is compared with responses from 256 humans on the Alternate Uses Task, and no person receives AI help. An Author Correction exists (doi 10.1038/s41598-024-54745-y).

candidates.title: The current state of artificial intelligence generative language models is more creative than humans on divergent thinking tasks
candidates.evidence: GPT-4 output is compared with responses from 151 humans on divergent thinking tasks, and no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: The Link Between Diverse Words and Original Ideas Is Weakening in the AI-Era College Admissions
other_versions: PsyArXiv jsz58 v5, titled 'The Creative Link Between Words and Ideas is Weakening in the AI Era'
candidates.evidence: A natural experiment compares essays from 372,793 applicants before and after ChatGPT, plus three controlled experiments, on the link between diverse words and original ideas. The report found no published version and gives no N or conditions for the experiments. It names only the first of 9 authors and cites the v8 DOI because the unversioned DOI returns 404.

candidates.title: Individual Gain, Collective Loss: Metacognitive Adaptation in AI-Assisted Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series 8(1), 700–705
candidates.evidence: A conceptual paper with no data. The arXiv abstract names six capacities and the AAAI abstract names seven.

candidates.title: Ex Ante Evaluation of AI-Induced Idea Diversity Collapse
candidates.task: idea generation, LLMs vs. unaided human baselines
candidates.evidence: The report classes this as model-only: three LLMs are compared with unaided human baselines, with no data on people using AI. The title frames the outcome as idea diversity collapse.

candidates.title: Seeing the Hivemind: A Consensus-Aware Interaction Technique for Mitigating AI Homogenization
candidates.evidence: A computational evaluation plus a user study (N = 16) tests a consensus-aware interaction technique for reducing AI homogenization. The report does not describe the user study's conditions, and arXiv lists the paper as in review.
